title: Why websites don't actually know your password
description: A well-built website never stores your real password. It stores a hash, a one-way fingerprint. Here's how that works and where it falls short.

scenes.say: Here's a strange fact. A properly built website doesn't actually know your password.

Instead, it stores a hash. A hash is a fingerprint made by a maths function. The same input always gives the same fingerprint. Change one letter, and it looks completely different. And you can't run it backwards.
When you log in, the site hashes what you typed and compares fingerprints. It never needs the original.
So if a site is breached, attackers get hashes, not passwords. Good sites add a random salt to each one, and use deliberately slow algorithms like Argon2.
But a hash isn't magic. Attackers can still guess common passwords, hash them, and compare. So a strong, unique password still matters. Follow for more plain text threats.
